---
title: "Linguistic data matrices"
---

[PHOIBLE 2.0](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.2593234) is a curated collection of phonological inventory records assembled from descriptive sources. Its [documentation](https://phoible.github.io/faq/) stresses that an inventory usually describes a doculect, that multiple inventories may share a Glottocode, and that some inherited inventories combine sources. We will thus call one row an **inventory record**, not a language.

The course copy is pinned to PHOIBLE 2.0 and follows the release's [download and citation guidance](https://phoible.org/download). It excludes tone entries and rows explicitly marked as marginal, then samples one inventory within each Glottocode. A cell equal to one means that a retained PHOIBLE value row links the inventory to the segment. A zero means **not listed under this preparation rule**. It does not establish that speakers never produce the corresponding phone.

## Defining the array and its indices

Let there be $n$ linguistic objects and $p$ measured variables. A data matrix is

$$
\mathbf X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}.
$$

Its entries are

$$
x_{ij}=\text{the value of variable }j\text{ for object }i.
$$

The complete row for object $i$ is

$$
\mathbf x_i^{\mathsf T}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
x_{i1}&x_{i2}&\cdots&x_{ip} \quad\text{(symbolic indices)} % dqr-allow: symbolic-derivation
\end{bmatrix},
$$

and the complete column for variable $j$ is

$$
\mathbf x_{\cdot j}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
x_{1j}&x_{2j}&\cdots&x_{nj} \quad\text{(symbolic indices)} % dqr-allow: symbolic-derivation
\end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf T}.
$$

A row asks how one inventory record is represented across segments. A column asks how one segment listing varies across inventory records. This is the earlier [unit-of-analysis decision](../foundations/linguistic-data.qmd) written in matrix form.

## Constructing the PHOIBLE matrix

The code below reproduces the row sample, the macroarea-stratified split, and the training-only column filter. The random seeds identify reproducible procedural choices; they are not linguistic measurements.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

phoible <- readRDS("data/phoible/phoible-pilot.rds")

select_one_inventory <- function(inventories, seed = 20260827L) {
  inventories <- inventories[
    order(inventories$glottocode, as.integer(inventories$inventory_id)),
  ]
  groups <- split(seq_len(nrow(inventories)), inventories$glottocode)
  RNGkind(sample.kind = "Rejection")
  set.seed(seed)
  keep <- vapply(
    groups,
    function(index) index[[sample.int(length(index), size = 1L)]],
    integer(1)
  )
  inventories[unname(keep), ]
}

make_split <- function(selected, seed = 20261018L) {
  area <- selected$macroarea
  area[is.na(area) | area == ""] <- "Unclassified"
  split <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(selected))
  set.seed(seed)
  for (name in sort(unique(area))) {
    index <- sample(which(area == name))
    n_validation <- floor(0.15 * length(index))
    n_test <- floor(0.15 * length(index))
    split[index[seq_len(n_validation)]] <- "validation"
    split[index[n_validation + seq_len(n_test)]] <- "test"
    split[index[is.na(split[index])]] <- "training"
  }
  factor(split, levels = c("training", "validation", "test"))
}

selected <- select_one_inventory(phoible$inventories)
selected$split <- make_split(selected)
training_ids <- selected$glottocode[selected$split == "training"]

memberships <- merge(
  phoible$memberships,
  selected[c("inventory_id", "glottocode")],
  by = c("inventory_id", "glottocode")
)
training_frequency <- table(
  memberships$segment_id[memberships$glottocode %in% training_ids]
)
retained_segments <- sort(names(training_frequency)[training_frequency >= 20L])

X <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = nrow(selected),
  ncol = length(retained_segments),
  dimnames = list(selected$glottocode, retained_segments)
)
listed <- memberships[memberships$segment_id %in% retained_segments, ]
X[cbind(
  match(listed$glottocode, rownames(X)),
  match(listed$segment_id, colnames(X))
)] <- 1

c(
  source_value_rows = phoible$provenance$original_value_rows,
  selected_inventory_records = nrow(X),
  retained_segment_columns = ncol(X),
  listed_cell_fraction = mean(X)
)
```

The resulting matrix has `r nrow(X)` inventory records and `r ncol(X)` segment columns. Of its `r format(length(X), big.mark = ",")` cells, `r scales::percent(mean(X), accuracy = 0.1)` are listed. This sparsity is a property of the prepared database matrix, not an estimate of how often phones occur in speech.

## Seeing rows and columns

The full matrix is too large to label. The following plot thus displays four training inventories from each classified macroarea and the twenty most common training segments. Every plotted cell is read directly from `X`.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

training_index <- which(selected$split == "training")
training_mean <- colMeans(X[training_index, , drop = FALSE])
areas <- setdiff(sort(unique(selected$macroarea)), c("", NA, "Unclassified"))

display_rows <- unlist(lapply(areas, function(area) {
  candidates <- training_index[selected$macroarea[training_index] == area]
  candidates <- candidates[order(rowSums(X[candidates, , drop = FALSE]))]
  candidates[unique(round(seq(1, length(candidates), length.out = 4)))]
}), use.names = FALSE)
display_columns <- order(training_mean, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(20)]

segments <- phoible$segments[
  match(colnames(X), phoible$segments$segment_id),
]
slice <- X[display_rows, display_columns, drop = FALSE]
plot_data <- as.data.frame(as.table(slice))
names(plot_data) <- c("glottocode", "segment_id", "listed")
plot_data$inventory <- selected$language_name[
  match(plot_data$glottocode, selected$glottocode)
]
plot_data$area <- selected$macroarea[
  match(plot_data$glottocode, selected$glottocode)
]
plot_data$inventory <- paste0(plot_data$inventory, " (", plot_data$area, ")")
plot_data$segment <- segments$segment[
  match(plot_data$segment_id, segments$segment_id)
]
plot_data$inventory <- factor(
  plot_data$inventory,
  levels = rev(unique(plot_data$inventory))
)
plot_data$segment <- factor(
  plot_data$segment,
  levels = segments$segment[display_columns]
)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = segment, y = inventory, fill = factor(listed))) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.15) + # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("0" = "white", "1" = "black"),
    labels = c("Not listed", "Listed"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(x = "Segment", y = "Inventory record") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

The cell in a particular row and column can now be interpreted only by using both index maps. The first displayed row, for instance, can be recovered without copying its values into the notes.

```{r}
first_displayed <- display_rows[[1]]
data.frame(
  glottocode = rownames(X)[first_displayed],
  inventory = selected$language_name[first_displayed],
  listed_retained_segments = sum(X[first_displayed, ])
)
```

## The representation constraint

Changing a row from an inventory record to a Glottocode-level average would change the observational unit. Changing the columns would change which segment contrasts are available. Repeating a column would give the corresponding listing pattern extra numerical weight. Matrix methods cannot infer that an omitted distinction was theoretically intended, nor can they recover within-source detail removed before construction.

Before factorization, record (i) the row unit, (ii) the row-selection rule, (iii) the column-retention rule, (iv) the cell coding, and (v) the collection to which those records belong. This **representation constraint** fixes the information available to every later operation.

## Checking the representation

1. What does $x_{ij}=1$ mean in this matrix?
2. Why is “not listed” safer than “absent” for $x_{ij}=0$?
3. Why is one sampled inventory record not necessarily one language?
4. Which part of the code prevents validation and test inventories from selecting columns?
5. What would change if the rows were individual PHOIBLE value records?

The [next page](centering-and-scaling.qmd) changes the origin and possible unit of each segment column while keeping these row and column definitions fixed.
